The theorem and polynomial bound are sound; the missing routine enumeration is repaired by querying all N_n <= n+q(n) nodes, including labels and constants. No statement or prerequisite changes.

F4 inaccurately restates layered syntax as a gate list. The actual QC14 full-list encoding and Clifford+T word convention already supply serial gate lists; singleton layers provide the immediate faithful interpretation. Corrected F4 and constructed singleton layers explicitly in 6.1. This representational omission does not invalidate the phase identity, compiler action or resource bounds.

F2 wrongly attributes uniformity to the general finite-probability definition. Uniform YES samples and independent runs are already explicit in Given and supplied by the Simon theorem and algorithm, so the count remains valid. Corrected F1/F2 and explicitly multiplied the four 1/4 probabilities before summing event weights in 2.1. This repairs a citation inaccuracy, not a false numerical conclusion.

Checked all six proof steps and the actual reversible procedure/cost proof, matrices, layered semantics and QC14 decoder. The integer phase is 4abc, seven phase gates plus eighteen CNOTs implement clean-scratch CCZ, and two Hadamards give Toffoli. Six gates implement X; fixed replacements preserve the displayed bound and clean work. Singleton layers and distinct target output indices now explicitly satisfy syntax and code. Statement unchanged; strict contract passed. This is a repair account, not independent review of my repair.

Checked the actual finite-space definition, independent-run algorithm, Simon sampling theorem and its complete proof. For s=01, orthogonality forces second coordinate zero and rank at most one. The three lines in V_2 give 3*16-3+1=46 failing four-tuples; independence and uniformity give weight 1/256 each, hence 23/128 and union bound 3/16. Exhaustive XOR-span enumeration confirms all 256 cases. Citation repair only, Example unchanged; strict contract passed. This is my repair account, not independent review of it.
